description.p: Operate a WVC210 network camera from the desktop without the vendor ActiveX pages. Connect over the LAN, watch the live stream, and move the camera with pan and tilt.
The app talks to one camera at a time using its HTTP CGI interface. Settings stay on this computer; preset poses are stored on the camera and restored if a reboot clears NVRAM.

ul.li: Live MJPEG view, plus MPEG/RTSP when libVLC is available
Pan, tilt, presets, patrol, and a user home pose
Setup pages for users, network, and video
Talkback with G.711 when the camera allows it

screenshot.caption: Live view with pan-tilt pad and presets

description.p: Linux Flatpak uses X11/XWayland from the GNOME app icon, a lowercase app id, and bundled libVLC for MPEG/RTSP. Preset Go, Patrol, and User home talk to the camera with preset=move again. Empty NVRAM slots are restored from AppData without rewriting poses the camera still has.
Live presets and user home are stored on this computer so Go, Patrol, and Home still work after a camera reboot clears NVRAM.
Adds live Patrol through occupied presets and per-slot Delete. Audio status follows the camera talk/listen mode.
First release: live view, PTZ, setup, talkback, and status for a single WVC210 camera.
